text: The production of concrete is one of the most significant contributors to global greenhouse gas emissions. This work focuses on bio-cementation-based products and their potential to reduce global warming potential (GWP). In particular, we address a proposed bio-cementation method employing bacterial metabolism in a two-step process of limestone dissolution and recrystallisation (BioZEment). A scenario-based techno-economic analysis (TEA) is combined with a life cycle assessment (LCA), a market model and a literature review of consumers’ willingness to pay, to compute the expected reduction of global GWP. Based on the LCA, the GWP of 1 ton of BioZEment is found to be 70–83% lower than conventional concrete. In the TEA, three scenarios are investigated: brick, precast and onsite production. The results indicate that brick production may be the easiest way to implement the products, but that due to high cost, the impact on global GWP will be marginal. For precast production the expected 10% higher material cost of BioZEment only produces a marginal increase in total cost. Thus, precast production has the potential to reduce global GWP from concrete production by 0–20%. Significant technological hurdles remain before BioZEment-based products can be used in onsite construction scenarios, but in this scenario, the potential GWP reduction ranges from 1 to 26%. While the potential to reduce global GWP is substantial, significant efforts need to be made both in regard to public acceptance and production methods for this potential to be unlocked.

text: Psittacid Adenovirus-2 (PsAdv-2) was identified in captive orange-bellied parrots (Neophema chrysogastor) during a multifactorial cluster of mortalities at the Adelaide Zoo, South Australia, and an outbreak of Pseudomonas aeruginosa septicaemia at the Tasmanian Department of Primary Industries, Parks, Water and Environment captive breeding facility, Taroona, Tasmania. This was the first time that an adenovirus had been identified in orange-bellied parrots and is the first report of PsAdv-2 in Australia. To investigate the status of PsAdv-2 in the captive population of orange-bellied parrots, 102 healthy birds from five breeding facilities were examined for the presence of PsAdv-2 DNA in droppings and/or cloacal swabs using a nested polymerase chain reaction assay. Additionally, eight birds released to the wild for the 2016 breeding season were similarly tested when they were recaptured prior to migration to be held in captivity for the winter. PsAdv-2 was identified in all breeding facilities as well as the birds recaptured from the wild. Prevalence of shedding ranged from 29.7 to 76.5%, demonstrating that PsAdv-2 is endemic in the captive population of orange-bellied parrots and that wild parrots may have been exposed to the virus. PsAdv-2 DNA was detected in both cloacal swabs and faeces of the orange-bellied parrots, but testing both samples from the same birds suggested that testing faeces would be more sensitive than cloacal swabs. PsAdv-2 was not found in other psittacine species housed in nearby aviaries at the Adelaide Zoo. The source of the infection in the orange-bellied parrots remains undetermined. In this study, PsAdv-2 prevalence of shedding was higher in adult birds as compared to birds less than one year old. Preliminary data also suggested a correlation between adenovirus shedding prevalence within the breeding collection and chick survival.

text: The growing grey seal (Halichoerus grypus) population in the Baltic Sea has created conflicts with local fisheries, comparable to similar emerging problems worldwide. Adequate information on the foraging habits is a requirement for responsible management of the seal population. We investigated the applicability of available dietary assessment methods by comparing morphological analysis and DNA metabarcoding of gut contents (short-term diet; n = 129/125 seals, respectively), and tissue chemical markers i.e. fatty acid (FA) profiles of blubber and stable isotopes (SIs) of liver and muscle (mid- or long-term diet; n = 108 seals for the FA and SI markers). The methods provided complementary information. Short-term methods indicated prey species and revealed dietary differences between age groups and areas but for limited time period. In the central Baltic, herring was the main prey, while in the Gulf of Finland percid and cyprinid species together comprised the largest part of the diet. Perch was also an important prey in the western Baltic Proper. The DNA analysis provided firm identification of many prey species, which were neglected or identified only at species group level by morphological analysis. Liver SIs distinguished spatial foraging patterns and identified potentially migrated individuals, whereas blubber FAs distinguished individuals frequently utilizing certain types of prey. Tissue chemical markers of adult males suggested specialized feeding to certain areas and prey, which suggest that these individuals are especially prone to cause economic losses for fisheries. We recommend combined analyses of gut contents and tissue chemical markers as dietary monitoring methodology of aquatic top predators to support an optimal ecosystem-based management.

text: The expansion of the grey seal (Halichoerus grypus) population in the Baltic Sea has intensified interactions with regional fisheries, mirroring global trends in predator–fishery conflicts. Effective management requires accurate assessment of foraging behavior, which we evaluated through a comparative analysis of dietary assessment techniques. Gut contents from 129 seals were analyzed using morphological methods, while 125 samples underwent DNA metabarcoding to determine short-term dietary composition. Concurrently, fatty acid (FA) profiles from blubber and stable isotope (SI) ratios in liver and muscle tissue (n = 108) provided mid- to long-term dietary signals. The methods yielded complementary data: morphological analysis identified prey at the species group level, while DNA metabarcoding enabled precise species-level identification, particularly for small or fragmented prey often overlooked. In the central Baltic, herring (Clupea harengus) dominated the short-term diet, whereas in the Gulf of Finland, percid and cyprinid species together constituted the primary prey. Perch (Perca fluviatilis) was a significant component in the western Baltic Proper. Liver SI values revealed distinct spatial foraging patterns and identified individuals likely to have migrated across regions. Blubber FA profiles differentiated seals with recurrent use of specific prey types, indicating dietary specialization. Notably, adult male seals exhibited FA and SI signatures suggestive of localized foraging specialization, implicating them as primary contributors to fishery impacts. These findings underscore the importance of integrating short-term gut content analysis with long-term tissue chemical markers to generate a comprehensive dietary profile. Such a combined approach offers a robust foundation for ecosystem-based management, enabling targeted mitigation strategies and informed conservation planning for apex marine predators in dynamic coastal systems.

text:
Ocular hypertension is a primary risk factor for glaucoma and results in retinal ganglion cell (RGC) degeneration. Current animal models of glaucoma lack severe RGC cell death as seen in glaucoma, making assessment of physiological mediators of cell death difficult. We developed a modified mouse model of ocular hypertension whereby long-lasting elevation of intraocular pressure (IOP) is achieved, resulting in significant reproducible damage to RGCs.

In this model, microbeads are mixed with hyaluronic acid and injected into the anterior chamber of C57BL/6J mice. text:
Decreased lung function is associated with non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), based on linking mechanisms such as insulin resistance and systemic inflammation However, its association with the risk of developing NAFLD is unclear. Our aim was to investigate whether baseline lung function is associated with incident NAFLD in middle-aged healthy Koreans.

A cohort study of 96,104 subjects (mean age: 35.7 years) without NAFLD were followed up from 2002 to 2015. NAFLD was diagnosed by ultrasound after the exclusion of other possible causes of liver diseases. Baseline percent predicted forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1%) and forced vital capacity (FVC%) were categorized in quartiles. Adjusted hazard ratios (aHR) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) (using the highest quartile as reference) were calculated for incident NAFLD at follow-up, controlling for covariates and potential confounders.

During 579,714.5 person-years of follow-up, 24,450 participants developed NAFLD (incidence rate, 42.2 per 1,000 person-years). The mean follow-up period was 5.9±3.4 years. Regardless of smoking history, the risk for incident NAFLD increased with decreasing quartiles of FEV1 (%) and FVC (%) in a dose-response manner (p for trend<0.001). In never smokers, the aHRs (95% CIs) for incident NAFLD were 1.15 (1.08–1.21), 1.11 (1.05–1.18), and 1.08 (1.02–1.14) in quartiles 1–3 for FEV1 (%) and 1.12 (1.06–1.18), 1.11 (1.05–1.18), and 1.09 (1.03–1.15) in quartiles 1–3 for FVC (%), compared with the highest quartile reference. Similar inverse association was present in smoke-exposed subjects (aHR for incident NAFLD were 1.14, 1.21, 1.13 and 1.17, 1.11, 1.09 across FEV1(%) and FVC(%) quartile in increasing order, respectively).

Reduced lung function was a risk factor for incident NAFLD in a large middle-aged Korean cohort with over half a million person-years of follow-up.

Reduced lung function is associated with an increased risk of incident non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) in a large cohort of middle-aged Korean adults. A prospective cohort study included 96,104 individuals without baseline NAFLD, with a mean age of 35.7 years, followed from 2002 to 2015. Decreased lung function is associated with non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), based on linking mechanisms such as insulin resistance and systemic inflammation However, its association with the risk of developing NAFLD is unclear. Our aim was to investigate whether baseline lung function is associated with incident NAFLD in middle-aged healthy Koreans.

A cohort study of 96,104 subjects (mean age: 35.7 years) without NAFLD were followed up from 2002 to 2015. NAFLD was diagnosed by ultrasound after the exclusion of other possible causes of liver diseases. Baseline percent predicted forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1%) and forced vital capacity (FVC%) were categorized in quartiles. Adjusted hazard ratios (aHR) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) (using the highest quartile as reference) were calculated for incident NAFLD at follow-up, controlling for covariates and potential confounders.

During 579,714.5 person-years of follow-up, 24,450 participants developed NAFLD (incidence rate, 42.2 per 1,000 person-years). The mean follow-up period was 5.9±3.4 years. Regardless of smoking history, the risk for incident NAFLD increased with decreasing quartiles of FEV1 (%) and FVC (%) in a dose-response manner (p for trend<0.001). In never smokers, the aHRs (95% CIs) for incident NAFLD were 1.15 (1.08–1.21), 1.11 (1.05–1.18), and 1.08 (1.02–1.14) in quartiles 1–3 for FEV1 (%) and 1.12 (1.06–1.18), 1.11 (1.05–1.18), and 1.09 (1.03–1.15) in quartiles 1–3 for FVC (%), compared with the highest quartile reference. Similar inverse association was present in smoke-exposed subjects (aHR for incident NAFLD were 1.14, 1.21, 1.13 and 1.17, 1.11, 1.09 across FEV1(%) and FVC(%) quartile in increasing order, respectively).

Reduced lung function was a risk factor for incident NAFLD in a large middle-aged Korean cohort with over half a million person-years of follow-up.
</source>

On November 29, 2004, Al-jazeera, an Arabic-language television channel based in Qatar, reported that the United States military used napalm during their attacks on Fallujah, Iraq. This account was made by Al-jazeera, and the report was not confirmed by major international news organizations based in the West.

In Ukraine, the president, Leonid D. Kuchma, proposed holding new elections to resolve the political crisis that was threatening the country. This suggestion was made by Kuchma in Kyiv and reported by the New York Times on the same day.

Romania’s elections, held on November 29, 2004, saw the ruling Social Democrat Party (PSD) come out ahead in both the legislative and presidential races. About 57 percent of all eligible voters participated, with roughly 18 million eligible voters in a population of 21.7 million.

Meanwhile, on November 29, 2004, Lycos Europe, an internet portal and email provider, introduced a screensaver aimed at increasing the operational costs for spammers by causing their websites to receive more traffic from voluntary user computers. This initiative by Lycos faces potential legal challenges.

Later that month, United States President George W. Bush began his first official visit to Canada, traveling to Ottawa as part of a regional engagement.

In Asia, China signed an agreement with the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) to establish the world’s largest free trade area. Potential members under consideration included Japan, South Korea, New Zealand, India, and Australia. The ASEAN group consists of countries such as Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Philippines, Thailand, Vietnam, Laos, Cambodia, and Myanmar, as well as Brunei Darussalam.

On November 30, 2004, in the United States, Congress reversed protections for wilderness areas. Through amendments to a large omnibus spending bill, Congress removed or nullified the effects of three court decisions that had expanded wilderness protections in Alaskan, Idaho, and coastal Georgia areas. This action was described as part of the 108th Congress’s final steps of the term and was criticized by advocacy groups such as Wilderness Watch and Public Employees for Environmental Responsibility (PEER).

In Northern Ireland, there were rising hopes that the political stalemate over the implementation of the Good Friday Agreement could be resolved through high-level talks. British Prime Minister Tony Blair was expected to meet with Democratic Unionist leader Ian Paisley at Downing Street, a developing prospect at the time.

text:
Figures released by the U.S. 2010 census on Wednesday show that the city of Detroit has lost approximately 238,270 people, one-fourth of its total, since 2000. Detroit, once one of the top five U.S. cities in population, has its lowest number of residents since 1910.

Population numbers affect the the amount of federal and state funding a city receives. In the last few decades, dozens of Michigan state laws have been passed allowing Detroit, because its population was at least 750,000, special measures to raise revenue and allocating it a larger share of Michigan's state revenue than its population warranted. Now that Detroit's population has fallen to 713,777, it is no longer eligible for these financial advantages.

The mayor of Detroit, Dave Bing plans to appeal the census results. He says more than 35,000 residents were not counted.

Detroit was the fifth largest U.S. city in 1950. The decline of the auto industry hastened the population loss already diminished by the 1967 riots that precipitated white flight to the suburbs. Approximately 23 percent of the city’s living quarters are now empty. To reduce the city's size there is a program in progress to demolish 10,000 abandoned or vacant buildings and turn the land into farms or countryside by 2014.

Detroit's congressional power has been steadily decreasing. It already lost one congressional seat since the 1980s.

U.S. federal laws forbid drawing congressional district boundaries that dilute minority voting strength. The 2000 redistricting rules for the 2012 elections mandated that Detroit's two congressional districts must be 60 percent black voters, since four out of five of Detroit's residents are black. To comply, the two remaining congressional districts will have to expand into Detroit's mostly white suburbs to attain enough minority voters to meet the 60 percent target, reducing the clout of black Detroit.

According to the 2010 U.S. census, Detroit has lost roughly 238,270 residents since 2000—a decline that has dropped the city’s population to 713,777, its lowest level since 1910. This significant contraction marks a sharp fall from when Detroit was one of the nation’s top five largest cities in 1950. The drop has serious implications for local and state funding, as cities with lower populations receive less in federal and state resources. Historically, Detroit qualified for special revenue-raising powers and a larger share of Michigan’s state budget because its population remained above 750,000. However, with the current population well below that threshold, the city no longer qualifies for these advantages.

Detroit’s mayor, Dave Bing, has expressed doubts about the census figures, suggesting that more than 35,000 residents may have been missed in the count. The city’s population decline is linked to the collapse of the auto industry and the mass exodus of white residents after the 1967 riots, which led to substantial “white flight” to the suburbs. About a quarter of Detroit’s housing stock is now vacant, and the city is moving forward with plans to demolish over 10,000 abandoned buildings, with the goal of turning large tracts of land into farmland by 2014.

As a result of its shrinking numbers, Detroit’s political influence is waning. The city has already lost a congressional seat since the 1980s, and its remaining districts are being redrawn under federal rules that require significant black voter representation due to the area’s demographic makeup. To comply with these redistricting requirements for the 2012 elections, Detroit’s congressional districts now have to include large portions of surrounding suburbs to achieve the mandated 60 percent minority voter threshold, further diminishing the city’s electoral clout.

On December 14th, after a single reading, the EU Parliament passed the Data Retention directive. 378 parliamentarians voted in favour of the Directive, 30 abstained and 197 voted against.

Significant aspects of this law are the lack of special measures for security and privacy of the collected data, lack of any rule as to how costs are to be reimbursed. Such measures had been proposed as amendments, but the block vote in Parliament (following a deal between the leaders of the two largest parties, the Christian democrat-conservative European People's Party and the Party of European Socialists, and the European Commission) rejected these amendments.

Partially, the law harmonises existing practice, allowing police forces to rely on retention of data for their investigations. In certain countries, privacy laws that mandated the destruction of such data after six months have hindered investigations. Poland, following one such case, wanted a 15 year data retention period.

Other commentators have noted that the EU produces vast numbers of directives, about ten per month, and most of these get passed into national law only very slowly. Ireland and Germany have stated that they will take this directive to the European Court of Justice. However, that will not prevent other countries from implementing it in a more or less severe form.

Italy has, in the last few months, been closing cybercafes that do not keep strict records of the identity of every user. It is such indicators that have convinced many privacy advocates that this law is not about terrorism at all, but about monitoring and controlling civil society.

The European Parliament approved the Data Retention Directive on December 14th during a single reading, with 378 members supporting the measure, 30 abstaining, and 197 opposing. A key feature of the law is its omission of specific protections for data security or privacy, as well as the absence of clear guidelines for who bears the costs of data storage. These elements had been suggested as amendments but were excluded due to a consensus between the leaders of the European People’s Party and the Party of European Socialists, along with the European Commission. 

The directive primarily aligns existing practices, permitting authorities to retain digital communications for investigative purposes. However, it does not establish uniform standards, leaving member states discretion to implement the requirements in varying ways. Some countries, such as Poland, previously imposed longer retention periods due to investigations impeded by shorter destruction timelines mandated by local privacy legislation. 

Critics and commentators have pointed out that the EU frequently enacts new directives, many of which take time to be adopted at the national level. Countries like Italy have already implemented strict user-identity logging requirements in public internet access points, prompting privacy advocates to argue that the new directive appears more focused on surveillance and societal control than on combating terrorism.

text:
Someone said to be an informant within Abu Musab al-Zarqawi's trusted circle told Coalition forces the insurgent leader was going to have a meeting, it has emerged. This information appears to have led US F-16Cs to a safehouse in the Iraqi town of Hibhid, where the Jordanian and five others, including a child, were killed on Wednesday.

The informer is said to want the insurgency to pursue a strategy within the Iraqi political process, which in the informer's view was in contrast to tactics executed by al-Zarqawi's leadership that involved ethnic killings.

It was one of the last in a long line of breadcrumbs leading the hunt for the Iraqi government's most-wanted murderer to the doorstep of an attractive isolated house in Hibhid.

In a late-April video al-Zarqawi had been shown spraying bullets from a machine gun with a horizon in the background. This is said to have revealed the general location of al-Zarqawi, found near Diyala province, in the north east of Iraq. The ethnically mixed region had seen an upsurge in violence and over days preceding the airstrike.

Murders had included a number of decapitated heads left in fruitboxes. Al-Zarqawi had been known for kidnapping and video beheadings of westerners in Iraq.

Another al-Zarwaqi insider also had given vital clues to the investigators before the final tip-off. A former customs clearance officer in Rutba identified as Ziad Khalaf al-Karbuli had named Sheikh Abu Abdul-Rahman as al-Zarqawi's spiritual advisor and gave-up contact details.

Ziad Khalaf al-Karbuli had appeared on Jordanian television, May 23, to confess his links to al-Zarqawi, and to his murder of a Jordanian driver and his kidnap of two Moroccan embassy employees in 2005. The vital clue about Abu Abdul-Rahman was not broadcast.

The US search for the Sheikh included the use of remote controlled aircraft, it was revealed.

However; it is said neither the al-Karbuli information nor the al-Zarqawi betrayer lead the Americans to press the fire button on al-Zarwaqi's two-story home. Al-Zarqawi was hard to catch because he reportedly eschewed trackable cell-phones in favour of high-tech Thuraya-made satellite phones to communicate.

The death certificate was signed by the secret informant who said both Sheikh Abu Abdul-Rahman and al-Zarqawi would be in Hibhid, Wednesday night.

For the elusive insurgent who had previously escaped attempts to bomb him, the execution came after comparison of this source's information with tracks of the location of satellite phone users.

The location found was beside a property with a courtyard surrounded by fields away from other buildings. It appears then the US command made the decision to strike at an address in the small town, near Baqubah.

US special forces were on the scene to photograph the dead al-Zarqawi at 6:17 p.m., two minutes after two 500lb bombs were dropped. Al-Zarqawi was said to be alive and being given medical assistance when he died of wounds sustained in the bombing.

Coalition forces received information suggesting Abu Musab al-Zarqawi was planning a meeting in the Iraqi town of Hibhid. According to a source within al-Zarqawi’s inner circle, an informant warned the United States about the anticipated encounter. This tip reportedly led to a military operation in which US F-16 fighter planes were deployed. In the ensuing air strike, a safehouse in Hibhid was hit. The raid resulted in the deaths of Jordanian fighters, five others, and a child.

The informant, said to be part of al-Zarqawi’s trusted circle, apparently advocated for the insurgency to pursue political participation within Iraq’s political framework—contrasting with what the informant described as al-Zarqawi’s leadership’s more violent tactics, which involved the use of ethnic killings and attacks such as decapitations.

This sequence of intelligence contributions marks another incremental step for the international manhunt targeting al-Zarqawi, who remains one of the most wanted terrorist leaders in the world. Previous leaks indicated that clues from allies and informants—including a former Iraqi customs officer, Ziad Khalaf al-Karbuli, who confessed on Jordanian television and provided details about al-Zarqawi’s spiritual adviser—had helped narrow the search. However, according to the latest account, those prior leads may not have directly led to the final operation that struck Hibhid.

US investigators reportedly employed remote-controlled aerial vehicles as part of their intelligence-gathering efforts prior to the bombing. Despite the valuable information from multiple sources—including an earlier tip about al-Zarqawi’s likely use of satellite communications technology—US command authorities apparently did not act on the Hibhid intelligence until it was corroborated with satellite phone usage data.

The target compound in Hibhid, described as a two-story house set in a courtyard surrounded by open fields, was attacked just after 6:17 p.m. on Wednesday. The attack involved two 500-pound explosive devices, and US special forces were present to document the scene. Initial reports indicate that al-Zarqawi was alive and receiving medical care at the time but succumbed to his injuries shortly after the strike.

The death of al-Zarqawi ends a prolonged and complex manhunt characterized by his evasion of detection through the use of advanced satellite communications and his penchant for choosing remote, secure locations. The chain of intelligence—ranging from direct insiders to satellite tracking and aerial surveillance—demonstrates the persistent challenges faced by anti-terrorism forces in tracking high-value targets.

This intelligence appears to have led U.S. F-16 fighter jets to a safehouse in the Iraqi town of Hibhid. The informant is said to advocate that the insurgency adopt strategies within Iraq’s political process, as opposed to the more violent tactics—such as ethnic killings—that al-Zarqawi’s leadership reportedly favored. This tip formed part of a series of leads that have progressively narrowed the hunt for al-Zarqawi to a small, secluded house in Hibhid.

The pursuit of al-Zarqawi has been marked by a trail of hints. In late April, a video showing al-Zarqawi using a machine gun was released; analysts believe this helped locate him near Diyala province in northeastern Iraq. The region, which is ethnically mixed and has experienced a surge in violence, had seen a rise in attacks in the days before the recent airstrike.

Al-Zarqawi was notorious for extreme violence, including the public display of decapitated heads inside fruit boxes and the kidnapping and beheading of foreigners. A former member of his circle—Ziad Khalaf al-Karbuli, a former Rutba customs officer—had previously identified Sheikh Abu Abdul-Rahman as al-Zarqawi’s spiritual advisor but this sensitive information was not made public.

Al-Karbuli himself confessed on Jordanian television in May 2005 to his role in murders and abductions connected to al-Zarqawi, but the details he shared proved less decisive in the final operation. The U.S. intelligence effort reportedly included the use of unmanned aerial vehicles in the search.

Despite these leads—including the information from al-Karbuli and another informant—the U.S. command apparently did not act on them when it received the most recent and specific tip about a meeting in Hibhid, likely based on satellite tracking of al-Zarqawi’s use of a hard-to-trace satellite phone.

According to accounts, the informant who provided the final information stated that both Sheikh Abu Abdul-Rahman and al-Zarqawi were expected in Hibhid that night. Intelligence analysts compared the location with known satellite phone pings, leading them to a two-story house in a rural courtyard setting outside a nearby village, close to Baqubah.

U.S. special forces were already at the scene when the attack occurred. At 6:17 p.m., two 500-pound bombs were dropped, killing al-Zarqawi. It is reported that he was alive and receiving medical care at the time but succumbed to his injuries shortly after the bombing.

text:
In image processing, a Gabor filter, named after Dennis Gabor, is a linear filter used for texture analysis, which essentially means that it analyzes whether there is any specific frequency content in the image in specific directions in a localized region around the point or region of analysis. Frequency and orientation representations of Gabor filters are claimed by many contemporary vision scientists to be similar to those of the human visual system. They have been found to be particularly appropriate for texture representation and discrimination. In the spatial domain, a 2-D Gabor filter is a Gaussian kernel function modulated by a sinusoidal plane wave (see Gabor transform).
Some authors claim that simple cells in the visual cortex of mammalian brains can be modeled by Gabor functions. Thus, image analysis with Gabor filters is thought by some to be similar to perception in the human visual system.

text: In image processing, a Gabor filter—named after Dennis Gabor—is a linear filter used to analyze texture by detecting specific patterns of frequency and orientation within a localized area of an image. This method helps determine whether certain spatial frequencies appear in particular directions around a given point. The way Gabor filters represent frequency and orientation is considered by many vision scientists to resemble how the human visual system processes information. Because of this similarity, they are especially effective for identifying and distinguishing textures. Mathematically, a 2-D Gabor filter combines a Gaussian envelope with a sinusoidal wave, forming a mathematical structure known as the Gabor transform. Some researchers suggest that the responses of simple cells in the visual cortex of mammals can be modeled using Gabor functions. As a result, using Gabor filters in image analysis may mimic aspects of human visual perception.

Machine vision (MV) is the technology and methods used to provide imaging-based automatic inspection and analysis for such applications as automatic inspection,  process control, and robot guidance, usually in industry. text:
In statistics and natural language processing, a topic model is a type of statistical model for discovering the abstract "topics" that occur in a collection of documents. Topic modeling is a frequently used text-mining tool for discovery of hidden semantic structures in a text body. Intuitively, given that a document is about a particular topic, one would expect particular words to appear in the document more or less frequently: "dog" and "bone" will appear more often in documents about dogs, "cat" and "meow" will appear in documents about cats, and "the" and "is" will appear approximately equally in both. A document typically concerns multiple topics in different proportions; thus, in a document that is 10% about cats and 90% about dogs, there would probably be about 9 times more dog words than cat words. The "topics" produced by topic modeling techniques are clusters of similar words. A topic model captures this intuition in a mathematical framework, which allows examining a set of documents and discovering, based on the statistics of the words in each, what the topics might be and what each document's balance of topics is.
Topic models are also referred to as probabilistic topic models, which refers to statistical algorithms for discovering the latent semantic structures of an extensive text body. In the age of information, the amount of the written material we encounter each day is simply beyond our processing capacity. Topic models can help to organize and offer insights for us to understand large collections of unstructured text bodies. Originally developed as a text-mining tool, topic models have been used to detect instructive structures in data such as genetic information, images, and networks. They also have applications in other fields such as bioinformatics and computer vision.

text:
Topic models represent a statistical approach to uncovering underlying themes within large collections of text. In both statistics and natural language processing, these models analyze documents to identify the main topics each text addresses, based on the frequency of words used. The central idea is that certain words tend to recur in documents centered on particular subjects—such as “dog,” “bone,” and “canine” for dog-related texts, and “cat,” “meow,” and “feline” for cat-focused ones. Importantly, a single document often addresses multiple topics, each contributing a specific proportion to its content. For instance, a document that is mostly about dogs but also covers cats might feature dog-related vocabulary roughly nine times more frequently than cat-related terms.

Mathematically, topic models encode this relationship by grouping similar words into clusters, which correspond to the abstract concepts or topics. This process allows analysts to assess which topics are prominent in a given document and to what extent they are balanced within it. Developed as a text-mining tool, these models can also be adapted for other data types, such as images or genetic data, due to their ability to detect latent semantic structures. Topic modeling’s versatility has led to its use in various domains, including bioinformatics and computer vision, where organizing and interpreting vast amounts of unstructured information is essential.

In statistics and natural language processing, a topic model is a statistical approach designed to identify the underlying topics present in a collection of documents. Topic modeling serves as a widely used text-mining technique for uncovering the hidden semantic structures within large bodies of text. The topics revealed by topic modeling correspond to clusters of related words. These models translate the statistical patterns of word usage across documents into mathematical representations, enabling analysts to detect and quantify which topics dominate each piece and how their proportions vary from document to document. Topic models provide a probabilistic framework for this process, allowing the identification of latent topics in extensive, unstructured text corpora.

Originally developed as a tool for text mining, topic models have expanded in application to other domains, such as genomics, image analysis, and network studies. Their versatility has also led to use in fields like bioinformatics and computer vision, where they help make sense of large, complex datasets by revealing the underlying themes or structures.

text:
In economics, perfect information (sometimes referred to as "no hidden information") is a feature of perfect competition. With perfect information in a market, all consumers and producers have complete and instantaneous knowledge of all market prices, their own utility, and own cost functions.
In game theory, a sequential game has perfect information if each player, when making any decision, is perfectly informed of all the events that have previously occurred, including the "initialization event" of the game (e.g. the starting hands of each player in a card game).
Perfect information is importantly different from complete information, which implies common knowledge of each player's utility functions, payoffs, strategies and "types". A game with perfect information may or may not have complete information.
Games where some aspect of play is hidden from opponents - such as the cards in poker and bridge - are examples of games with imperfect information.

text:
In economics, perfect information is a key feature of perfect competition. It's like everyone in the market has a magical app that shows all prices instantly, and they know exactly what they want (that's the utility bit) and how much it costs them to produce or buy stuff. Everyone's on the same page, no secrets.

Now, in game theory, a sequential game has perfect information if players know everything that's happened before they make a move. Like in chess, you can see the whole board and all the moves that came before. But here's the kicker: perfect info isn't the same as complete info. Complete info means everyone knows what everyone else wants and their strategies. A game can have perfect info but not complete info.

Take poker, for instance. You don't know what cards your opponents have, so it's a game of imperfect information. It's all about the unknowns.

text: Nita and Kit start to fight about the solution to the pollution in Jones Inlet, leading Nita to start to work on her own for a while. In the meantime, Nita's mother falls ill and is taken to the hospital with a brain tumor. Meanwhile, Kit finds out that his dog, Ponch, is able to create universes out of nothing, bringing in a lot of research possibilities where they can explore. Nita begins to practice with kernels - magical "software" that describes and reflects the surrounding area- in order to try to save her mother's life. While practicing, Nita meets a wizard named Pralaya who might be able to join her in saving her mother's life. She then discovers that the wizard may be overshadowed by the Lone Power, making it a dangerous prospect for them to work together. She discusses it with Kit, who decides to help her as well. While her mother is in surgery, Nita enters her body with Pralaya and begins to search for the kernel in order to kill the cancer, leaving Kit behind. Kit, using the universes Ponch creates, is able to also enter Mrs. Callahan's body to aid Nita and her mother. He helps her undo the deal she was in the process of making with the Lone Power for her mother's life, but she is still unable to eliminate all of the cancer. As the Lone Power is gloating in his anticipated victory, Nita's mother is able to take control of the kernel and defeat the Lone Power. She realizes that if she were to cure herself, she would be starting down a path at the end of which nothing would matter to her except extending her life, so she chooses to live out what life is left to her in love.

While she focuses on her own efforts, Nita’s mother suddenly falls seriously ill and is rushed to the hospital, a diagnosis revealing a brain tumor. But Pralaya warns her that working with him might be risky, as the powerful Lone Power could overshadow or control him. After weighing the dangers together, Kit agrees to join Nita’s quest. As her mother prepares for surgery, Nita, with Pralaya’s aid, enters her body and sets out to find and destroy the cancer’s kernel. Kit, using the limitless universes Ponch can spawn, manages to enter Mrs. Callahan’s body as well, standing by Nita’s side in the critical moment.

Together, they confront the sinister deal Nita had almost made with the Lone Power to secure her mother’s life. Despite their teamwork, fully eradicating the cancer proves out of reach. Just as the Lone Power basks in the thought of being defeated, Nita’s mother regains agency over the very kernel itself. She chooses, in that crucial instant, not to prolong her life at the cost of losing what truly matters: the chance to live her remaining days with meaning and love.

text:
Noise reduction is the process of removing noise from a signal. Noise reduction techniques exist for audio and images. Noise reduction algorithms may distort the signal to some degree. Noise rejection is the ability of a circuit to isolate an undesired signal component from the desired signal component, as with common-mode rejection ratio.
All signal processing devices, both analog and digital, have traits that make them susceptible to noise. Noise can be random with an even frequency distribution (white noise), or frequency-dependent noise introduced by a device's mechanism or signal processing algorithms.
In electronic systems, a major type of noise is hiss created by random electron motion due to thermal agitation. These agitated electrons rapidly add and subtract from the output signal and thus create detectable noise.
In the case of photographic film and magnetic tape, noise (both visible and audible) is introduced due to the grain structure of the medium. In photographic film, the size of the grains in the film determines the film's sensitivity, more sensitive film having larger-sized grains. In magnetic tape, the larger the grains of the magnetic particles (usually ferric oxide or magnetite), the more prone the medium is to noise. To compensate for this, larger areas of film or magnetic tape may be used to lower the noise to an acceptable level.

Noise reduction is the process of removing noise from a signal. Noise reduction techniques exist for audio and images. Noise reduction algorithms may distort the signal to some degree. Noise rejection is the ability of a circuit to isolate an undesired signal component from the desired signal component, as with common-mode rejection ratio.
All signal processing devices, both analog and digital, have traits that make them susceptible to noise. Noise can be random with an even frequency distribution (white noise), or frequency-dependent noise introduced by a device's mechanism or signal processing algorithms.
In electronic systems, a major type of noise is hiss created by random electron motion due to thermal agitation. These agitated electrons rapidly add and subtract from the output signal and thus create detectable noise.
In the case of photographic film and magnetic tape, noise (both visible and audible) is introduced due to the grain structure of the medium. In photographic film, the size of the grains in the film determines the film's sensitivity, more sensitive film having larger-sized grains. In magnetic tape, the larger the grains of the magnetic particles (usually ferric oxide or magnetite), the more prone the medium is to noise. To compensate for this, larger areas of film or magnetic tape may be used to lower the noise to an acceptable level.
</source>

Marcia Hubbard, still attached to Bartley, confines herself to her father's home in Equity, Maine, from which she never leaves. Bartley, on the other hand, has died. Ben Halleck stands hesitantly, unable to determine whether or not he should seize the chance and propose to her.

text:
The European Parliament passed the Data Retention Directive on December 14th in a single vote. It received 378 votes in favor, 30 abstentions, and 197 against. The law lacks explicit safeguards for data security or privacy, and it does not define who is responsible for funding data storage. These points had been proposed as amendments but were dropped after a consensus formed between the European People’s Party, the Party of European Socialists, and the European Commission.

The directive codifies current practices by allowing law enforcement to retain digital communications for investigative use. Yet it fails to set consistent standards, leaving each member state to determine how to apply the rules. In Poland, retention periods were previously extended because shorter timelines under local privacy laws had disrupted ongoing investigations.

Observers note that the EU often introduces new directives, but national implementation is slow. Italy already enforces strict logging of user identities at public internet access points. Critics argue this directive reflects a broader shift toward surveillance and social oversight, not just counter-terrorism. The emphasis appears less on preventing attacks than on enabling continuous monitoring of digital activity across member states.

text: Bio-cementation presents a tangible path toward lowering the global warming potential (GWP) of concrete, a major contributor to carbon emissions. This study focuses on BioZEment, a method that harnesses bacterial activity through a two-stage process: dissolving limestone and subsequently recrystallizing it into a stable binder. The assessment combines scenario-based techno-economic analysis (TEA), life cycle assessment (LCA), a market model, and a review of existing research on consumer pay-willingness. The LCA shows that producing one ton of BioZEment reduces GWP by 70 to 83 percent compared to standard concrete. Three production pathways were examined: brick manufacturing, precast fabrication, and on-site application. Brick production, while technically simplest to implement, faces economic constraints that limit its global impact. Precast use, which adds 10 percent to material cost, could lower GWP from concrete production by up to 20 percent, depending on scale and deployment. On-site application, though hindered by technical challenges in handling and consistency, holds potential for GWP reductions between 1 and 26 percent. These outcomes suggest BioZEment could play a measurable role in decarbonizing construction, but only if production processes are refined and public confidence in the material is established.

The initiative raised questions about liability under anti-spam laws, particularly regarding unintended consequences.

Later that month, President George W. Bush traveled to Ottawa for his first state visit to Canada. The trip was part of a broader diplomatic push across North America.

In Asia, China finalized a framework agreement with the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) to create the largest free trade zone in history. The changes, inserted as riders to the omnibus measure, were seen by environmental groups like Wilderness Watch and Public Employees for Environmental Responsibility (PEER) as a deliberate undermining of federal conservation efforts. The move was among the final legislative actions of the 108th Congress.

In Northern Ireland, a new opening emerged in the stalled implementation of the Good Friday Agreement. British Prime Minister Tony Blair was set to meet with Democratic Unionist Party leader Ian Paisley at Downing Street, a development that signaled a shift in the fragile political momentum.

text: In economics, perfect competition relies on the assumption of perfect information—each agent knows all relevant prices and production costs, and can assess their own preferences and willingness to pay with precision. This isn’t a literal app, but a theoretical condition where no one holds an informational advantage. In game theory, a sequential game has perfect information when each player observes all prior actions, as in chess, where the full history of moves is visible. Still, perfect information does not imply complete information. Knowing what has happened isn't the same as knowing what others desire or how they will act. A game may unfold with perfect recall of past moves yet remain incomplete in terms of payoffs or strategies. Poker illustrates this clearly: players see the community cards and prior bets, but not opponents’ hands. The uncertainty lies not in the sequence of moves, but in what others hold and plan to do. This gap defines imperfect information, not a flaw in observation, but a structural limit on knowledge.

text: The grey seal (Halichoerus grypus) population in the Baltic Sea has grown steadily, increasing pressure on local fisheries—a pattern seen elsewhere in marine systems where predators and fishing activities overlap. To understand how seals use available prey, we compared three dietary assessment methods. Gut contents from 129 seals were examined using traditional morphological techniques, identifying prey remains at the species group level. DNA metabarcoding was applied to 125 samples, revealing species-level details, especially for small or degraded prey that morphological analysis often misses. Parallel analysis of fatty acid (FA) profiles from blubber and stable isotope (SI) ratios in liver and muscle (n = 108) provided longer-term dietary signals. In the central Baltic, herring (Clupea harengus) made up most of the short-term diet. In the Gulf of Finland, percid and cyprinid fish together were primary food sources. Perch (Perca fluviatilis) was a major component in the western Baltic Proper. Liver SI values showed differences in foraging locations, with some individuals likely moving between regions. Blubber FA profiles highlighted patterns of repeated prey use, suggesting dietary specialization in certain seals. Adult males displayed FA and SI signatures consistent with focused foraging in localized areas, implying they are disproportionately involved in fishery interactions. Combining short-term gut data with long-term chemical markers captures a fuller picture of dietary habits. This integrated approach supports practical management decisions, allowing for targeted actions and better planning in coastal zones shaped by shifting predator-prey dynamics.

While she works, her mother collapses at home—taken to the hospital with a brain tumor confirmed by MRI and biopsy. Over days, the dog produces new configurations of space, not just in theory but as actual, stable alternate structures—real universes, not illusions.

Nita turns to magical kernels, small crystalline objects that record and replay aspects of reality. She tests them on the inlet, on her mother’s illness. One kernel, shaped like a sparrow’s bone, begins to respond to her focus, mirroring neural pathways in her mother’s brain. She brings it to Pralaya, a wizard who moves through the city like a shadow, known only through whispers. He confirms the kernel’s potential but warns of the Lone Power—its reach extends into the space between thoughts, and it may already have touched him.

Kit agrees to help after weighing the risk. With Ponch’s new ability to spawn universes on command, Kit finds a way into Mrs. Callahan’s body through a thin, unstable link. Nita, guided by Pralaya, enters first—her mother’s body mapped in fragments of memory and sensation. They find the cancer not as a growth, but as a kernel shaped like a cracked mirror, humming with borrowed power.

The Lone Power almost wins—its voice murmurs through the mind, offering a clean cure, a return to health. But Nita’s mother, aware now, refuses. Not for survival, but for choice. She lets go of the kernel. The moment the system resets, the cancer collapses inward. No victory, no miracle—just stillness. And peace.

text: Noise reduction strips away unwanted signal elements to sharpen clarity, used in both audio and image processing. The methods applied often reshape the original signal, occasionally adding artifacts in the process. Noise rejection describes a circuit's ability to isolate useful signals from interference—measured, for example, by common-mode rejection ratio. All signal systems, analog or digital, face noise because of physical limits and operational imperfections. Some noise spreads evenly across frequencies—called white noise—while other forms concentrate in specific bands, stemming from component behavior or processing steps. In electronics, hiss arises from thermal motion of electrons, creating small, random shifts in output that accumulate into audible interference. In photographic film, noise appears as grain, and its size dictates performance: larger grains capture more light but make the image appear grainy. Similarly, magnetic tape uses particles like ferric oxide or magnetite; larger ones pick up more signal but also increase noise. To manage this, systems may use larger film frames or longer tape sections, spreading the signal over more material so noise becomes less prominent—effectively raising the signal-to-noise ratio to a usable level.

text: Psittacid Adenovirus-2 (PsAdv-2) surfaced during a mortality event involving captive orange-bellied parrots (Neophema chrysogastor) at Adelaide Zoo, South Australia, and was concurrently linked to a Pseudomonas aeruginosa septicaemia outbreak at the Tasmanian Department of Primary Industries, Parks, Water and Environment facility in Taroona. This represents the first documented detection of any adenovirus in the species and the first report of PsAdv-2 in Australia. To determine the virus’s distribution, 102 healthy parrots from five breeding facilities were screened for PsAdv-2 DNA using a nested polymerase chain reaction assay on droppings and/or cloacal swabs. Eight birds released for the 2016 breeding season were also tested upon recapture prior to winter housing. The virus was present in all five breeding facilities and in every wild-recaptured bird, indicating persistent transmission within the captive population. Shedding rates ranged from 29.7% to 76.5%, confirming the virus is established in the population and that wild birds have been exposed. Faecal samples yielded more positive results than cloacal swabs, suggesting greater sensitivity in detecting the virus in faeces. PsAdv-2 was not detected in other psittacine species housed alongside the parrots at Adelaide Zoo, indicating minimal cross-species transmission under these conditions. The infection source remains unidentified. Adults showed higher shedding prevalence than birds under one year old. Early data suggest a possible inverse relationship between adenovirus shedding levels in breeding groups and chick survival, though this pattern requires further validation.

text:
Topic models are statistical tools for revealing hidden themes across large bodies of text. Rather than relying on pre-defined categories, they identify clusters of words that frequently co-occur in documents—patterns that signal underlying subjects. For example, a cluster including “dog,” “paw,” and “bark” points to a discussion about dogs, while another with “cat,” “whisker,” and “purr” suggests a focus on cats. These word groupings aren't rigid; a single document may contain elements of several topics, with each contributing differently to its overall content. A piece mostly about dogs might mention feline-related terms only occasionally—perhaps a third as often as dog-specific vocabulary—reflecting a shift in emphasis rather than equal balance.

The models assign numerical weights to each topic within a document, showing how much of a given text relates to each theme. Words are grouped not by meaning alone, but by their combined presence across documents, forming abstract topics like "pet behavior" or "animal anatomy." This approach doesn't require labels or human tagging. Because the method relies on statistical patterns in word usage, it extends beyond text. Researchers have applied it to image analysis, where pixel patterns resemble word co-occurrence, and to gene expression data, where certain gene combinations mirror topic clusters. Its strength lies in extracting structure from raw, unorganized information—whether that’s a million blog posts, millions of DNA sequences, or a database of scanned photographs.

Frey walks out of the Ohio county jail into a stiff autumn wind and heads straight for Chicago. He doesn’t stop to consider the distance, the weather, or the state of his clothes. His mind is fixed on Lilly. She’s been alone since her grandmother died—alone in the halfway house, alone in the silence that follows someone you’ve loved being gone. The novel begins not with a flourish but with the quiet weight of that absence.

Lilly had been in the same recovery program Frey attended—back when he was still in the system, and she was just trying to stay upright. They met in a room with folding chairs and a water-stained ceiling, both of them learning how to hold a sentence together without breaking. He remembers her voice, low and careful, like she was testing each word before letting it go.

When Frey arrives in Chicago, the halfway house director gives him the news without flinching: Lilly is dead. She took her own life a week earlier. No note. No warning. Just gone. He doesn’t cry. He walks to a liquor store on the edge of the neighborhood, flips through bottles, and buys the cheapest wine he can find—six dollars, flat, no label. He carries it back to the empty room he’s been given, sits on the edge of the bed, and stares at the bottle. He doesn’t open it.

He calls Leonard. They’d known each other in the treatment center, not close, not friends—just two men who’d watched the same people vanish. Frey had once said he’d look after him. Leonard, now on the phone, says he’ll hold Frey to that. He demands thirty thousand dollars. But not for himself. He wants Frey to promise that one day he’ll explain what he did with the money. And he wants Frey to promise that if he ever opens the wine, he’ll call first.

Frey doesn’t know how to keep those promises. He spends the next few months moving through spaces that don’t fit him—job interviews that end in silence, apartments that smell like old plastic and not enough light. He trusts people who vanish, listens to advice that leads nowhere. He stays quiet when he should speak, stays still when he needs to move.

Two years pass. Leonard stops answering. Then, a letter: he’s sick. Not just sick—AIDS, late stage. He says he’s going to stop taking his medication. No formal goodbye. Just the words: *I’m doing it because I don’t want to be a burden.*

Frey doesn’t drink the wine. He doesn’t call. He sits in the same chair, looking at the bottle, and waits. Not for anything. Just for the shape of time to settle.

Mayor Dave Bing has questioned the accuracy of the census data, noting that more than 35,000 people might not have been counted.

Political power has also waned. Detroit has not held a congressional seat since 1980, and its remaining districts have been redrawn under federal redistricting rules. These rules mandate substantial minority representation, particularly Black voters, due to the city’s demographic profile. For the 2012 elections, the new district boundaries had to incorporate large portions of suburban areas to reach the 60 percent minority voter threshold. text: In image processing, a Gabor filter—named for Dennis Gabor—is a linear tool designed to detect localized patterns of frequency and orientation within an image. It identifies how certain spatial frequencies cluster in specific directions near a point. This approach mirrors how the human visual system extracts texture information, making it effective for distinguishing textures. The filter's structure combines a Gaussian-shaped envelope with a sinusoidal wave, forming what is known as the Gabor transform. Some studies indicate that the responses of simple cells in the mammalian visual cortex can be approximated using Gabor functions. As a result, applying Gabor filters in image analysis may reproduce certain features of human perception.

Among 96,104 middle-aged Korean adults without NAFLD at baseline, reduced lung function predicted a higher risk of developing non-alcoholic fatty liver disease over time. The cohort, followed from 2002 to 2015, had a mean age of 35.7 years. NAFLD was confirmed by abdominal ultrasound after ruling out other causes of liver disease. Pulmonary function was measured using FEV1% and FVC%, each divided into quartiles based on predicted values. Adjusted hazard ratios (aHR) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated using the highest quartile as reference, with adjustments for age, sex, body mass index, blood pressure, lipid levels, glucose, alcohol intake, physical activity, and smoking status.

text: Noise reduction removes unwanted signal elements to enhance clarity, applied in both audio and image processing. This process often alters the original signal, sometimes introducing artifacts. Noise rejection measures a circuit's capacity to distinguish useful signals from interference, quantified, for instance, by the common-mode rejection ratio. All signal systems, whether analog or digital, contend with noise due to physical constraints and operational imperfections. Noise can be evenly distributed across frequencies, known as white noise, or concentrated in specific bands, resulting from component behavior or processing steps. In electronics, thermal motion of electrons generates hiss, producing small, random output fluctuations that accumulate into audible interference. Photographic film exhibits noise as grain, with larger grains capturing more light but increasing image graininess. Magnetic tape utilizes particles like ferric oxide or magnetite; larger particles enhance signal capture but also amplify noise. To mitigate this, systems may employ larger film frames or longer tape sections, distributing the signal over more material to reduce noise prominence and improve the signal-to-noise ratio.

BioZEment, a bio-cementation method, offers a promising approach to reducing concrete's global warming potential (GWP). This technique utilizes bacterial activity in a two-stage process: dissolving and then recrystallizing limestone into a stable binder. The study evaluates BioZEment through techno-economic analysis (TEA), life cycle assessment (LCA), a market model, and consumer pay-willingness research. Producing one ton of BioZEment can reduce GWP by 70 to 83 percent compared to conventional concrete.

Three production pathways were analyzed: brick manufacturing, precast fabrication, and on-site application. While brick production is technically straightforward, economic limitations restrict its global impact. Precast use, which increases material costs by 10 percent, could reduce concrete production GWP by up to 20 percent, depending on scale and deployment. On-site application, despite technical challenges in handling and consistency, could achieve GWP reductions ranging from 1 to 26 percent.

These findings indicate that BioZEment could significantly contribute to decarbonizing the construction industry. However, realizing this potential requires refining production processes and building public confidence in the material.

On December 14, the European Parliament passed the Data Retention Directive in a single vote, with 378 votes in favor, 30 abstentions, and 197 against. The directive does not include explicit safeguards for data security or privacy, nor does it specify who is responsible for funding data storage. These issues were proposed as amendments but were removed after a consensus was reached between the European People’s Party, the Party of European Socialists, and the European Commission.

The directive formalizes existing practices by permitting law enforcement to retain digital communications for investigative purposes. However, it does not establish consistent standards, leaving each member state to decide how to implement the rules. In Poland, retention periods were previously extended because shorter timelines under local privacy laws had disrupted ongoing investigations.

Implementation of EU directives often lags at the national level. Italy, for instance, already enforces strict logging of user identities at public internet access points. Critics view this directive as part of a broader trend toward increased surveillance and social oversight, rather than solely counter-terrorism measures. The focus seems to be more on continuous monitoring of digital activity across member states than on preventing specific attacks.

text:
The grey seal population in the Baltic Sea has increased steadily, raising concerns about its impact on local fisheries. To assess how seals utilize available prey, we employed three dietary assessment methods. Traditional morphological techniques identified prey remains at the species group level from the gut contents of 129 seals. DNA metabarcoding, applied to 125 samples, provided species-level details, particularly for small or degraded prey that morphological analysis often overlooks. Additionally, fatty acid (FA) profiles from blubber and stable isotope (SI) ratios in liver and muscle (n = 108) offered insights into longer-term dietary habits.

In the central Baltic, herring (Clupea harengus) dominated the short-term diet. In the Gulf of Finland, percid and cyprinid fish were the primary food sources. Perch (Perca fluviatilis) was a major component in the western Baltic Proper. Liver SI values indicated variations in foraging locations, suggesting that some seals move between regions. Blubber FA profiles revealed patterns of repeated prey use, hinting at dietary specialization among certain seals. Adult males exhibited FA and SI signatures consistent with focused foraging in localized areas, implying a disproportionate involvement in fishery interactions.

Combining short-term gut data with long-term chemical markers provides a comprehensive view of dietary habits. This integrated approach aids in practical management decisions, facilitating targeted actions and better planning in coastal zones influenced by shifting predator-prey dynamics.

text: In economics, perfect competition assumes perfect information: every agent knows all relevant prices and production costs and can precisely assess their own preferences and willingness to pay. This theoretical condition means no one holds an informational advantage. Game theory applies a similar concept to sequential games. Perfect information in these games means each player observes all prior actions, as in chess, where the complete history of moves is visible. However, perfect information does not equate to complete information. Knowing past actions differs from understanding others' desires or future actions. A game can have perfect recall of past moves but remain incomplete regarding payoffs or strategies. Poker exemplifies this: players see community cards and prior bets but not opponents' hands. The uncertainty stems not from observing moves but from unknown hands and plans. This gap defines imperfect information, representing a structural knowledge limit, not an observational flaw.

text:
Topic models are statistical tools that uncover hidden themes in large text collections. They detect clusters of words that often appear together, indicating shared subjects. For instance, words like "dog," "paw," and "bark" signal a topic about dogs, while "cat," "whisker," and "purr" suggest a focus on cats. These word groups are flexible; a document may blend multiple topics, with varying emphasis. A text primarily about dogs might include some feline terms, but these would appear less frequently, perhaps a third as often as dog-related words, showing a difference in focus.

The models assign numerical weights to each topic within a document, quantifying the relevance of each theme. Words are grouped based on their co-occurrence across documents, forming abstract topics like "pet behavior" or "animal anatomy." This method requires neither labels nor human input. Since it relies on statistical patterns, its use extends beyond text. Researchers have applied topic modeling to image analysis, where pixel patterns resemble word co-occurrence, and to gene expression data, where gene combinations mirror topic clusters. The approach excels at extracting structure from raw, unorganized data, whether it consists of a million blog posts, millions of DNA sequences, or a database of scanned photographs.

text: Gabor filters, named after Dennis Gabor, are linear tools used in image processing to detect localized patterns of frequency and orientation. They identify spatial frequencies clustered in specific directions near a point, similar to how the human visual system extracts texture information. The filter's structure consists of a Gaussian-shaped envelope combined with a sinusoidal wave, creating the Gabor transform. Studies suggest that the responses of simple cells in the mammalian visual cortex can be approximated using Gabor functions. Applying these filters in image analysis may therefore replicate aspects of human perception.

text:
In a study of 96,104 middle-aged Korean adults without NAFLD at baseline, reduced lung function was linked to a higher risk of developing non-alcoholic fatty liver disease. The participants, with a mean age of 35.7 years, were tracked from 2002 to 2015. NAFLD diagnoses were confirmed through abdominal ultrasound after excluding other liver disease causes. Pulmonary function was assessed using FEV1% and FVC%, each divided into quartiles based on predicted values.

Over 579,714.5 person-years of follow-up, 24,450 participants developed NAFLD, translating to an incidence rate of 42.2 per 1,000 person-years. The mean follow-up period was 5.9 ± 3.4 years. The risk of NAFLD increased steadily with lower FEV1% and FVC% across quartiles, demonstrating a clear dose-response relationship (p for trend < 0.001).

Among never smokers, adjusted hazard ratios (aHR) for the lowest three quartiles of FEV1% were 1.15 (95% CI 1.08–1.21), 1.11 (1.05–1.18), and 1.08 (1.02–1.14). For FVC%, the corresponding values were 1.12 (1.06–1.18), 1.11 (1.05–1.18), and 1.09 (1.03–1.15). Similar patterns were observed in those with prior smoking exposure: aHRs for FEV1% were 1.14, 1.21, and 1.13 across the lowest three quartiles; for FVC%, they were 1.17, 1.11, and 1.09. This data suggests that lower baseline lung function independently predicts a higher risk of NAFLD, irrespective of smoking history.

text:
Frey left the Ohio county jail and walked into an autumn wind, heading for Chicago without hesitation. Distance, weather, and his disheveled appearance were of no consequence. His focus was on Lilly, who had been alone since her grandmother's death. She lived in a halfway house, surrounded by silence following the loss of someone she loved. The story begins with this quiet absence.

Lilly had been part of the same recovery program Frey attended during his time in the system. She was trying to stay afloat, and they met in a room with folding chairs and a water-stained ceiling, both learning to hold sentences together without falling apart. Frey recalls her voice, low and deliberate, as if she tested each word before speaking it.

Upon arriving in Chicago, the halfway house director delivered the news without emotion: Lilly had taken her own life a week prior. There was no note, no warning, just an abrupt absence. Frey showed no tears. He went to a nearby liquor store, browsed the bottles, and purchased the cheapest wine available—a six-dollar bottle with no label. He took it back to his empty room, sat on the bed, and stared at the bottle, leaving it unopened.

He then called Leonard, someone he had known from the treatment center. They weren't close, but they had shared the experience of watching others disappear. Frey had once promised to look after Leonard. On the phone, Leonard demanded Frey fulfill that promise, asking for thirty thousand dollars. However, the money wasn't for himself. Leonard wanted Frey to promise to one day explain what he did with the money and to call him if Frey ever decided to open the wine.

Frey was unsure how to keep these promises. Over the next few months, he drifted through spaces that didn't suit him—job interviews ending in silence, apartments smelling of old plastic and lacking light. He trusted people who disappeared and followed advice that led nowhere. He remained quiet when he should have spoken and still when he needed to move.

Two years passed, and Leonard stopped answering his calls. Then, a letter arrived: Leonard was sick—not just sick, but with late-stage AIDS. He announced he would stop taking his medication, stating, "I'm doing it because I don't want to be a burden."

Frey didn't drink the wine. He didn't call. He sat in the same chair, looking at the bottle, waiting—not for anything specific, just for time to pass.

text:
Nita and Kit clash over Jones Inlet, polluted with chemicals and sediment. Their disagreement drives a wedge between them; Nita decides to act alone. During this time, her mother suffers a collapse at home, diagnosed with a brain tumor after MRI and biopsy. Concurrently, Kit notices something unusual about his dog, Ponch: a distortion in the air, a peculiar bending of light nearby. Over several days, Ponch begins creating actual, stable alternate spatial configurations—entire universes, not mere illusions.

Nita explores magical kernels, crystalline objects that capture and replay aspects of reality. She experiments with them on Jones Inlet and her mother's illness. One kernel, resembling a sparrow's bone, reacts to her concentration, reflecting neural patterns in her mother's brain. She seeks out Pralaya, a reclusive wizard known only through rumors. He validates the kernel's potential but cautions about the Lone Power, which intrudes between thoughts and may have already contacted him.

Kit, after assessing the risks, agrees to assist. Using Ponch's ability to generate universes, Kit accesses Mrs. Callahan's body through a fragile, unstable connection. Nita, directed by Pralaya, enters first, navigating her mother's body through fragments of memory and sensation. They discover the cancer, not as a tumor but as a kernel shaped like a cracked mirror, pulsating with stolen energy.

The Lone Power nearly prevails, its voice whispering promises of a cure and restored health. However, Nita's mother, now aware, refuses. Her choice is not for survival but for autonomy. She releases the kernel. As the system resets, the cancer implodes. There is no triumph, no miracle—only stillness. And peace.

text: Curcumin, a polyphenolic compound with anti-inflammatory properties and low toxicity, is often studied in relation to inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). However, in C57Bl/6 and BALB/c mice fed an iron-sufficient diet and exposed to dextran sodium sulfate to induce colitis, oral curcumin supplementation led to mild anemia, reduced iron stores in the liver and spleen, worsened colonic inflammation, and decreased survival rates. These effects occurred consistently in both mouse strains, indicating that the impact is not dependent on genetic background. Curcumin's iron-chelating ability likely reduces systemic iron availability, which may counteract its anti-inflammatory effects in this context. While curcumin might influence IBD pathology through inflammation suppression, its effect on iron metabolism poses concerns for patients already at risk of iron deficiency. Therefore, using curcumin as a supplement in IBD requires regular monitoring of iron levels and blood counts to prevent exacerbating anemia.

text: Psittacid Adenovirus-2 (PsAdv-2) emerged during a mortality event among captive orange-bellied parrots (Neophema chrysogastor) at Adelaide Zoo, South Australia, coinciding with a Pseudomonas aeruginosa septicaemia outbreak at a facility in Taroona. This marked the first detection of any adenovirus in this species and the first report of PsAdv-2 in Australia. To assess the virus's spread, 102 healthy parrots from five breeding facilities were tested for PsAdv-2 DNA using a nested PCR assay on droppings and/or cloacal swabs. Eight birds released for the 2016 breeding season were also tested upon recapture. The virus was found in all five facilities and in every recaptured bird, indicating persistent transmission within the captive population. Shedding rates ranged from 29.7% to 76.5%, confirming the virus's establishment in the population and exposure in wild birds. Faecal samples produced more positive results than cloacal swabs, suggesting higher detection sensitivity in faeces. PsAdv-2 was not found in other psittacine species housed with the parrots at Adelaide Zoo, suggesting limited cross-species transmission. The infection source remains unknown. Adults exhibited higher shedding prevalence than birds under one year old. Initial data hint at a possible inverse relationship between adenovirus shedding levels in breeding groups and chick survival, though this requires further investigation.

Psittacid Adenovirus-2 (PsAdv-2) surfaced during a mortality event involving captive orange-bellied parrots (Neophema chrysogastor) at Adelaide Zoo, South Australia, and was concurrently linked to a Pseudomonas aeruginosa septicaemia outbreak at the Tasmanian Department of Primary Industries, Parks, Water and Environment facility in Taroona. This represents the first documented detection of any adenovirus in the species and the first report of PsAdv-2 in Australia. To determine the virus’s distribution, 102 healthy parrots from five breeding facilities were screened for PsAdv-2 DNA using a nested polymerase chain reaction assay on droppings and/or cloacal swabs. Eight birds released for the 2016 breeding season were also tested upon recapture prior to winter housing. The virus was present in all five breeding facilities and in every wild-recaptured bird, indicating persistent transmission within the captive population. Shedding rates ranged from 29.7% to 76.5%, confirming the virus is established in the population and that wild birds have been exposed. Faecal samples yielded more positive results than cloacal swabs, suggesting greater sensitivity in detecting the virus in faeces. PsAdv-2 was not detected in other psittacine species housed alongside the parrots at Adelaide Zoo, indicating minimal cross-species transmission under these conditions. The infection source remains unidentified. Adults showed higher shedding prevalence than birds under one year old. Early data suggest a possible inverse relationship between adenovirus shedding levels in breeding groups and chick survival, though this pattern requires further validation.

text: Kelley Winslow, a teenager performing off-Broadway in New York, steps into the lead role of *A Midsummer Night’s Dream* after the original actress injures herself. Her initial rehearsal is disjointed: lines forgotten, rhythm faltering, and an early exit from the theater. She seeks refuge in Central Park, not to flee, but to find solitude and commit her lines to memory. Meanwhile, Sonny Flannery, a Janus guard monitoring the threshold between the mortal world and the Otherworld, detects irregularities at The Gate. He perceives Kelley not as a girl, but as a Firework—vibrant, fleeting, and pulsating with an unfamiliar energy. Intrigued, he follows her. She becomes aware of his presence, turns abruptly, and accuses him of stalking her. When he continues advancing, she strikes him—a full, unhesitating blow. He is thrown across the grass. As she observes the aftermath, light erupts from her hands, flickering before stabilizing into raw, ungoverned energy. Sonny witnesses this. She departs, breath rapid, hands trembling. Shortly after, another Janus guard arrives. Sonny inquires if he saw anything. The guard hesitates, then responds, “Might have.” Kelley already senses she is teetering on the brink. Then, she learns the truth: she was never human. Born in the Otherworld, she was taken as an infant and concealed among mortals. Sonny’s confirmation of her origins shatters her reality. The border between the realms begins to deteriorate.
